transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
Hello! I'm Dora, and I'm here to help answer any questions you might have about your cataract surgery or your recovery. 

Do you have any questions for me today?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Hi Dora! Yes, I do have some questions. My first one is, when can I start doing a little bit of gardening?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
Great question! You can start doing light exercise like gardening about 1 week after your surgery. However, you should avoid any strenuous or heavy exercise for about a month.

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Thanks for the information! Yes, I do have another question. When can I start using my eye gel for dry eyes?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
That's a good question. If you were using eye gel or drops for dry eyes before your operation, it's safe to continue using them unless you've been told otherwise by your doctor.

If you're not sure about your specific eye gel, I'd recommend checking with your GP or care team to make sure it's okay to use.

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Thanks, that's very helpful! I do have another question. I'm very sensitive to bright light. Is that normal?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
It's quite normal for your eyes to be a bit sensitive to light as they adjust to your new lenses. If it's mild and things just seem brighter than you're used to, I'd recommend wearing sunglasses when you go outside.

However, if you have significant pain in bright light, or if your eye is also red and painful, that's not normal and we may need to check that further. In that case, do let us know.

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Thank you, wearing sunglasses sounds like a good idea. I have one more question. Should I still have some blurriness by now?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
That depends on how long it's been since your surgery. It's quite common for vision to not be completely clear in the first week after your operation, but it should improve quickly and settle down over time.

If your vision is still blurry or getting significantly worse, we may need to check it to make sure everything is okay.

How long ago was your surgery?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: It's been about a week since my surgery. Thank you for all the explanations. I don't have any more questions right now.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Brilliant! So just to confirm - have all your questions been answered today?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Yes, all my questions have been answered. Thanks so much for your help!

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: You're very welcome! I'm glad I could help. Take care and wishing you a smooth recovery!

verdict.label: pass
